body:
A rare case where the sequel is a shade better and makes an excellent impression. The director Jaspal Singh Sandhu and actors Sanjay Mishra, Neena Gupta have been repeated and they have performed very well indeed in their respective fields. The narrative is smooth and riveting establishing some good storytelling.

The plot. A simple natured middle aged male prison guard ( Sanjay Mishra) develops a soft corner for a female inmate ( Neena Gupta) who is serving time. They manage to meet regularly and spend time together after working hours. Things are smooth till she gets involved in a serious incident and he helps her out because of which both land in serious trouble with the law.

The director has done a superb job in making an engrossing movie. There is enough of suspense, mystery and a few scenes are chilling too. The moral --legal dichotomy is presented well and is thought provoking. As Sanjay Mishra says there is a difference between a killing and a vadh. Clearly the highlight of the movie are the understated and mature performances of the lead couple who make everything they do so believable. Amitt K Singh as the investigating officer and Kumud Mishra as the jail Superintendent have acted well in the supporting cast lending realism to the characters.

Vadh 2 is a rare treat where the performances are so "Royal" they almost make up for a lack of suspense. If you are a seasoned thriller fan, you will likely guess every plot twist and character reveal before the interval.

However, the cast is a 10/10 masterclass. Sanjay Mishra and Neena Gupta can turn a simple conversation into high end drama with just their expressions. I was also very impressed by the natural acting of Amitt K Singh, Yogita Bihani, and Akshay Dogra, along with the always excellent Shilpa Shukla and Kumud Mishra.

The production is stylish, and the song "Ishq ki Umar" at the ending is absolutely beautiful. Even though I outsmarted the script in the first 20 minutes, the sheer quality of the acting made it impossible to look away. Come for the performances, not the mystery.

The first half sets up the story with a villain who has an absolutely insane mindset, instantly pulling you into the film. But unfortunately, it struggles to maintain that same intensity and depth as the story progresses.

The second half, however, redeems things quite well. It becomes gripping and cleverly connects all the dots, making the narrative feel more complete and engaging.

Overall, it's a decent watch-definitely worth a one-time watch 👍

It is the strong ensemble cast that shows the true grit of the movie on an otherwise predictable plot.

I mean the moment we saw that hand drawn carriage featuring again in this part we knew what happened to the protagonist. Through glimpses in a slow moving first half we could also guess who might be the killer.

So inspite of a very good premise since the who how and what were predictable, that took away a lot of credibility from a thriller.

Vadh 2 doesn't try to recreate the shock of the first film, and that works in its favour. Instead of relying on twists, it leans into moral tension and quiet dread. The story feels heavier and more reflective, rooted in consequence rather than revenge. It learns from its predecessor and builds suspense well, delivering an edge-of-the-seat thriller by the end. It's good to see Bollywood reaching its potential without making noise about it.

The performances are restrained and convincing, with a calm menace that makes even simple scenes feel loaded. The film takes its time, and when it turns dark, it feels earned. While it isn't as sharp as Vadh, it's more mature in tone. The only drawback is that the protagonist's backstory needed a bit more depth.

A thoughtful sequel that chooses depth over shock and mostly lands.
